chapters.overview: Heading of a section of a project case study, also listed in the chapter index and the ⌘K palette. Short: one to three words.
chapters.statement: Heading of the section that states the problem the project solved. Short: one to three words.
chapters.stack: Heading of the section listing the languages, frameworks, libraries and tools the project is made with. Short: one to three words, as in 'Built with'.
stack.groups.tooling: Heading of a group of tiles: the test runners, linters and services used to build and ship the project. Keep it short.
stack.version: Read by screen readers only, before a software version number such as 16.4.6. {version} is that number.
stack.derived: A small note under the tiles: the version numbers are read automatically from the project's dependency lockfile when the site is published, not typed by hand.
hero.eyebrow: A small all-capitals line above the project name: category · year · role. Keep the ' · ' separators and the order of the three placeholders unless your language needs another order.
hero.eyebrowShort: The same small line without the role: category · year. Keep the ' · ' separator.
hero.linksLabel: Screen-reader name of the group of the project's outbound links. {name} is the project's name, which is never translated.
hero.liveDemo: A link. The words inside <sr>…</sr> are read only by screen readers; keep the tag, and keep the visible words first so voice-control users can say them.
hero.source: A link to the code on GitHub. Keep 'GitHub' as written. The words inside <sr>…</sr> are read only by screen readers; keep the tag, and keep the visible words first.
facts.timelineOngoing: A date range that has not ended. {start} is a month and year already formatted for your language.
facts.timelineRange: A date range. {start} and {end} are a month and year already formatted for your language.
gallery.region: Screen-reader name of a horizontally scrollable strip of screenshots. It starts with the visible section heading, {title}; keep {title} first.
index.nav: Name of the list of a page's sections (the chapter index). One word if possible.
index.position: Shown on a small button on phones: which section the reader is in. {n} and {total} are numbers.
index.skip: A link for keyboard users that appears when focused and jumps to the chapter index.
palette.section: Heading of a group of commands in the ⌘K command palette that act on the project page being read.
palette.jump: A command in the ⌘K palette that scrolls to a section. {title} is the section's heading.
outcomes.derived: A small note under a row of figures: the numbers are computed automatically from the code when the site is published, not written by hand.
stack.lead: A small note above the list of programming languages used in the project's repository. 'GitHub' stays as written.
